$comment: MACHINE half of what the responder leaves for the rest of the platform (agents/coordinator/responder-argo.yaml respond, post-session); the HUMAN half is responder-verdict.md. The machine block's own shape is agents/issue_body.py's; this file names the keys the responder writes into it. Spike (2026-11-07): nothing imports this file.

issue_lines.description: the lines a triage session writes into the ONE issue it may file (title `🚨 <alertname>: <summary>`); the shell upserts alert-fp, self-referential, fix-verdict and Touches into the machine block, legacy lines kept

alert_fp.description: the read-back key across every claimed repo

subject.description: ONE per thread — the thread's identity (a related-but-different subject files fresh and links)

touches.description: the narrowest write surface (ADR-097); omitted when unknown; a codeowner-author verdict is ONE sentence in the body, never a line

cause.description: same repo only; anything else is not bound

fix_verdict_ring.description: POST <agent-loop eventsource>/fix-verdict — rung after agent-fix on a `fix` verdict, not inside an observation window; fix-debounce decides the set

last_cleared_line.description: the ONE line a clear rewrites on a thread that stays open

remediation_would_line.description: REMEDIATION-WOULD: <verb> <namespace>/<kind>/<name> — <reason>; line-anchored, independent of the fix verdict (POSIX class syntax as the shell's jq test uses it)

verdict.description: the recorded verdict, `none` when the session filed nothing

raw.description: kept even when the line does not parse — still scored

remediation_would.description: one per DISTINCT marker line, in order; declared non-actions dropped; [] when none — scored into ../docs/remediation-would-scoreboard.md

claim_responder.description: the AgentStack claim's spec.responder (the claim island's XRD); rendered by the Composition into Role/RoleBinding agentstack-responder
